translation.text:
<warning>Faded red vermilion woodblock print; vertical Classical Mongolian script in the main text body and left margin cannot be reliably transcribed.</warning>
<meta>Pothi-format xylograph leaf from the Mongolian Kanjur printed in red ink within a double-ruled border; 25 vertical lines of Classical Mongolian text in the central panel, Mongolian foliation in the left marginal box, and Chinese title and foliation in the right marginal box.</meta>

<margin><unclear>4 vertical Mongolian marginal entries (section, volume, and folio markers), not transcribed</unclear></margin>
<margin>Sutra on the Precepts and Conduct of the <term>Vinaya</term> <gloss>monastic discipline</gloss> Masters, Volume 6, Upper Section, Folio 3 <note>original: "律師戒行經第六卷上三"; Chinese title and foliation marker printed in the right margin to guide bookbinders and printers when sorting Mongolian woodblock leaves</note></margin>
<unclear>25 vertical lines of Classical Mongolian text, not transcribed</unclear>

<summary>A vermilion woodblock leaf from the Mongolian Kanjur containing twenty-five vertical lines of untranscribed Classical Mongolian script. The right margin preserves a Chinese title and foliation marker identifying the text as the sixth volume, upper section, third folio of the Sutra on the Precepts and Conduct of the Vinaya Masters.</summary>
<keywords>Mongolian Kanjur, Classical Mongolian, Vinaya, monastic discipline, Sutra on the Precepts and Conduct of the Vinaya Masters, woodblock print, xylograph, bilingual foliation</keywords>
